description: GLP-1 receptor agonist trials (semaglutide, liraglutide) target T2DM patients with suboptimal glycaemic control despite existing therapy. CGM-based pre-screening identifies candidates with elevated mean glucose and suboptimal TIR who are most likely to respond to GLP-1 intensification. This protocol is T2DM specific — T1DM patients should be screened against the DIAMOND or closed-loop protocol.

inclusion_criteria.human_rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonists work via mechanisms specific to T2DM — they stimulate endogenous insulin secretion (beta-cell dependent) and suppress glucagon. These mechanisms are absent in T1DM where beta cells are destroyed. Enrolling T1DM patients would expose them to ineffective therapy and confound the trial results.
SUSTAIN-6 and PIONEER-6 enrolled patients with HbA1c ≥ 7.0–7.5%. Patients below this threshold have adequate control and are not candidates for intensification.
Patients with very high GMI (> 10.5%) often have severe insulin deficiency, active infections, or acute complications that must be managed before trial participation.
Identifies patients with suboptimal control — the target population for GLP-1 intensification. Well-controlled patients (TIR > 70%) are not appropriate candidates.
154 mg/dL corresponds approximately to HbA1c 7.0% (the ADA intervention threshold). Reinforces GMI criterion with a direct glucose measure — both must be met.

exclusion_criteria.human_rationale: T2DM patients on GLP-1 therapy have low hypoglycaemia risk when not on concurrent sulphonylureas or insulin. If a T2DM patient already has > 2 severe hypo events, they likely have complicating factors (advanced nephropathy, concurrent insulin) that require careful review before adding GLP-1 therapy.

notes: v2: Added diabetes_type == T2DM inclusion criterion. Based on Marso SP et al., Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes (SUSTAIN-6), NEJM 2016; and Husain M et al., Oral Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes (PIONEER-6), NEJM 2019.
